title: How is a file made?
question: A program creates a file on ext4 and writes to it. What does the file system do?

stops.note: The name is not there, and O_CREAT: ext4 makes the file, all in one journal transaction.
A free inode for it: found in a block group's inode bitmap, and marked used.
The name "new.txt": into free space in a block of the directory, next to the other names.
The bytes go into the page cache, and the page is marked dirty. Nothing is on the disk yet.
Delayed allocation: no disk block is chosen yet; one is only reserved.
The last reference to the open file goes. The file stays: it has a name.
